Progenitor

proh-JEN-i-tor · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Progenitor is an ancestor or parent; the originator of a line, idea, or movement.

Charles Darwin is often called the progenitor of modern evolutionary biology, though many of his ideas built on earlier naturalists' work.

Worked Example

The small startup is now considered the progenitor of an entire industry, having invented the technology that dozens of competitors later copied.

A progenitor is an ancestor or original source -- of a family line, an idea, or a movement -- here, the company that started an entire industry.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

ancestor: An ancestor is anyone you descend from, however far back — one name among many on the family tree. A progenitor is the one at the head of the line: the original ancestor or source from which everything afterward descends. Every progenitor is an ancestor, but most ancestors did not start the line.

originator: An originator deliberately creates or starts something new — a plan, a style, a rumor — and the word points at the act of invention itself. A progenitor is defined instead by what follows: a whole line of descendants, followers, or later versions that all flow from it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

descendant: a person or thing that comes after and derives from an earlier source

successor: a person or thing that follows and takes the place of another

Where it sits · how directly the line begins with them — influence → progenitor → patriarch

influence vs. progenitor: An influence simply has some effect on something later, without necessarily being its direct original source, unlike a true progenitor.

patriarch vs. progenitor: A patriarch is the founding father figure of an entire family or dynasty, an even more central, singular originating figure than a general progenitor.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — pro-

prefix — pro-: forward, before (Latin)

root — -gen-

root — -gen-: to beget, to produce, to give birth to (Latin gignere, genitus)

suffix — -itor

suffix — -itor: one who (as in editor, competitor) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Progenitor comes from Latin pro- ('before, forward') plus gignere/genitus ('to beget, to produce') and -itor, 'one who,' as in editor and competitor -- so a progenitor is literally 'the one who begets before,' the original source from which later generations or ideas descend.

Use the root in a new word: generate

Use the root in a new word: generate: Solar panels generate electricity by converting sunlight directly into usable power.

Word Choice

Progenitor is often paired with the word progeny (which you already learned) -- a progenitor is the original ancestor or source, while progeny are the descendants or offspring that come after.
